researchSummary: Authoritative evidence has been obtained confirming the composition of Alien Goddess by Mugler. The official Mugler brand sources (product page, scent-family category, brand editorial) and strong secondary sources (Fragrantica, Basenotes, retailer pages reproducing official copy) consistently confirm the MIP Gemini research values for all four critical composition fields (family, notes.top, notes.heart, notes.base). The legacy factory AI values are refuted across all sources. Recommended classification: R2 — targeted deterministic correction.
accessNotes: Direct HTTP access to mugler.com and fragrantica.com returned 403 Forbidden for all attempted URLs. Official Mugler product descriptions were obtained via Google search engine snippets that accurately index mugler.com page content. The ingredient names and family descriptions are consistent across multiple independent search queries and are corroborated by the successfully fetched REBL Scents retailer page, which reproduces official brand copy. The language is distinctively official brand terminology: 'Italian bergamot essence', 'jasmine grandiflorum', 'Madagascar bourbon vanilla', 'cashmeran wood'. Confidence in the accuracy of the official brand copy is HIGH despite the direct access limitation.
flankerExclusionNote: All evidence obtained pertains to the original Alien Goddess Eau de Parfum (2021). Flanker variants were actively excluded during research: Alien Goddess Intense (2022) and Alien Goddess Supra Florale (2023) appeared in search results and were not used as evidence sources. The Fragrantica URL used (alien-goddess-68354) is specifically the 2021 original EDP, distinct from Intense (74871) and Supra Florale (82489). No flanker evidence was admitted.

findings.notes: Official Mugler product page: 'a floral ambery woody creation'. Also confirmed by Mugler Mag article URL path which reads 'genesis-of-a-floral-amber-woody-perfume'. Mugler also categorises this fragrance under their 'Ambery' scent family browse category.

The Mugler Mag article's page title indexed by Google is 'Floral oriental woody perfume: a Goddess touch'. This uses 'oriental' rather than 'ambery'. The URL slug of the same article says 'floral-amber-woody-perfume'. Both terms are from official Mugler content for the same fragrance. Resolution: both confirm non-vanilla/non-fruity amber-family character. Mugler uses 'ambery' and 'oriental' as overlapping descriptors. This is an internal Mugler naming inconsistency, not a dispute about the fundamental character.
Mugler officially lists Alien Goddess under their 'Ambery' scent family browse category. This is the structural brand classification.

Fragrantica classifies Alien Goddess as 'Oriental Floral' — the traditional perfumery taxonomy term. 'Oriental Floral' and 'Floral Amber' overlap significantly in traditional perfumery vocabulary. The IFRA/industry 'Oriental' family corresponds closely to the modern 'Amber' family terminology used by many brands. This is a terminology mapping difference, not a factual dispute about the character of the fragrance.

Official Mugler product description: 'The first notes reveal a burst of bubbly Italian bergamot essence. Paired with an overdose of unexpected coconut water accord, the scent immediately releases a dazzling explosion of light.' Origin of bergamot (Italian) and form of coconut note (water accord, not milk) are explicitly stated by the brand.

Fragrantica normalised note names: Coconut Water and Bergamot (without 'Italian' or 'essence'/'accord' qualifiers). Consistent with official Mugler content. Fragrantica convention omits origin/form qualifiers.
Retailer confirms Bergamot Essence and Coconut Water. Consistent with official sources.

Official Mugler: 'At the heart of Alien Goddess resides a deeply sensual and feminine fusion of jasmine grandiflorum and heliotrope accord.' Mugler specifies Jasmine Grandiflorum explicitly — not Jasmine Sambac. The variety distinction is authoritative brand information.

Fragrantica normalised note names: Jasmine and Heliotrope (without the Grandiflorum variety qualifier). Consistent with official Mugler content. The 'Jasmine' in the MIP research value corresponds to Jasmine Grandiflorum in official Mugler language.
Retailer confirms Jasmine Grandiflorum and Heliotrope. Consistent with official Mugler language.

Official Mugler: 'an endless trail of addictive Madagascar bourbon vanilla, magnified by the vibrant and woody intensity of cashmeran wood.' Origin (Madagascar) and variety (Bourbon Vanilla) are explicitly stated by the brand.
Fragrantica normalised note names: Bourbon Vanilla and Cashmeran. Consistent with official Mugler content (minus the Madagascar origin qualifier).
Retailer confirms Bourbon Vanilla and Cashmeran. Consistent with official sources.
Launch year 2021 confirmed across all official and secondary sources without exception.
Mugler categorises this under 'womens-fragrances' in the URL path. Official description uses 'deeply sensual and feminine fusion'. Fragrantica also lists as 'a fragrance for women'.

Perfumers Nathalie Lorson and Marie Salamagne confirmed across Fragrantica (Tier 2), Basenotes (Tier 2), and multiple retailer sources. One search result snippet specified 'Firmenich perfumers Nathalie Lorson and Marie Salamagne'. A single secondary source used the spelling 'Nathalie Larson' — this appears to be a transcription error; Fragrantica uses 'Lorson'. MIP Gemini research had the correct attribution.

The official brand website and all 2021+ product launches use 'Mugler' (not 'Thierry Mugler'). The brand was rebranded from 'Thierry Mugler' to 'Mugler'; the exact year of the official name change could not be pinpointed from available sources but was completed before the Alien Goddess 2021 launch. Older retail sources still use 'Thierry Mugler'. MIP Gemini research sourceNotes correctly noted: 'Canonical name is Mugler Alien Goddess (formerly credited under Thierry Mugler).' The supplier list used 'Alien Goddess/ Thierry Mugler' — the 'Thierry Mugler' part is legacy naming. Current canonical brand: Mugler.

findings.notes: Mugler describes their note chapters using the terms: 'Radiant Revelation' (top), 'Miraculous Revelation' (heart), 'Mindful Revelation' (base). identifiedConflicts.resolution: Both are official Mugler. The URL slug uses 'floral-amber-woody'; the page title uses 'Floral oriental woody'. The structural category is 'Ambery'. All three agree the character is amber/oriental — not vanilla. The naming inconsistency is within Mugler's own editorial content and does not represent a dispute about the fundamental olfactory character. Resolution: Amber family confirmed; exact label is a Maison normalisation decision.

Fragrantica uses traditional perfumery classification 'Oriental Floral'. Mugler uses 'floral ambery woody'. Both describe the same olfactory character — a floral fragrance with a dominant amber/oriental character and woody base. 'Oriental' is the traditional industry term; 'Amber' is the modern brand term. These are complementary, not contradictory. Maison MKC vocabulary uses 'Amber' (not 'Oriental') as a family term. MIP research value ['Amber', 'Floral'] is the appropriate Maison-vocabulary normalisation of both official sources.

Official Mugler specifies 'Jasmine Grandiflorum'. Fragrantica normalises to 'Jasmine' (no variety). For the Maison MKC, the question is whether to use 'Jasmine' (matching Fragrantica normalisation and MIP research) or 'Jasmine Grandiflorum' (matching official Mugler precision). Recommended: 'Jasmine Grandiflorum' is the more precise and authoritative term. Founder decision required on Maison vocabulary preference.

resolutionRecommendation.rationale: Authoritative research clearly and consistently confirms the MIP Gemini research values for all four critical composition fields. The legacy factory values are refuted across multiple independent sources. R2 (targeted deterministic correction) is recommended over R4 (full regeneration) because: (1) the corrections are specific and factual — family, notes.top, notes.heart, notes.base, profile, and description require updating; (2) the existing Maison editorial content — subtitle 'Radiant Bloom', vibe tags, occasions, seasons, signatureStyle, intelligence scores — is qualitatively sound and appropriate for the confirmed amber-floral character; (3) regenerating the full record risks losing editorial quality that is well-authored; (4) R4 is reserved for records whose editorial and discovery knowledge is broadly compromised — this record's non-composition knowledge is not compromised.
